solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shelter inside as deluge inside's turning loud

indicators.note: the shelter word sits within the two letters for 'as', splitting them

parts.note: as can mean so ('as good' = 'so good')
a tent is a portable shelter

indicators.note: the inside of the deluge word turns about, its two middle letters trading places

parts.note: a deluge is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Someone sheltering indoors finds the rain hammering down noisily around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is SO here, and the deluge is the shelter-free rain whose inner pair is swapped by 'inside's turning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was the herald in Homer with a voice of fifty men, so a stentorian voice is extremely loud.

clue.text: 'Sun', that's good for reading, for men only

indicators.note: for means standing in place of, so the good letter takes the place of the reading letter

parts.note: the sun is an example of a star, hence the quotation marks around it
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs of basic schooling
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper read only by men, approved as decent reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Sun' is a definition by example of STAR, not the newspaper; G replaces its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is a celebration restricted to male guests, typically before a wedding.

clue.text: Shops one in interim without judge around

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside what remains
without means the judge word is taken away
around says the removed letters sit on both sides, T at the front and RY at the back

parts.note: an interim arrangement is a temporary one
to try a case is to judge it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stores open only for a short stopgap period, with no magistrate on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge word's letters sit around the rest of the interim word, one at the front and two at the back, so 'without judge around' strips both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is the Latin-style plural of emporium, a large store selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Still teaches English catching pen one dropped

indicators.note: catching means the outer letters grab and hold the pen word inside them
in a down clue, dropped means a letter is moved lower down the word

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
I is the Roman numeral one
a quill is an old-fashioned feather pen

explanation.surface: A calm instructor teaches English while holding a pen, having dropped something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'dropped' sends the one letter further down the teaching word, before the pen is caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To still someone is to calm or quieten them, which is what a sedative or soothing word does.

clue.text: Legislature as session includes judge again

indicators.note: includes says the answer is held within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: A parliament's sitting brings in a judge for a second hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Legislature, all of as and the start of session.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge or evaluate, and the re- prefix makes it a second evaluation.

clue.text: Dead fantastic bird about to flip compact

indicators.note: to flip is to turn over, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
the roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights
CA (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A legendary bird, now dead, turns over a powder case.
explanation.walkthrough: D + ROC + CA gives DROCCA, which 'to flip' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact is an agreement or treaty between parties, the same as an accord.

clue.text: Musical heroine doesn't open song

indicators.note: the heroine's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of The Sound of Music and West Side Story

explanation.surface: The leading lady of a show declines to start with a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Produce cotton on twig

definitions.meaning: to produce money from an asset
to cotton on is to come to understand something
to twig is informal British for to grasp or understand

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables, cotton, and a small branch: a list of farm goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions; 'produce' and 'twig' pose as nouns but are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: All three are verbs: realising a sum is producing it, and realising a fact is cottoning on to it or twigging it.

clue.text: Needle before admitting past transgression being over

indicators.note: admitting means letting the following pieces in, so they go inside

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-natal
ago means in the past

indicators.note: being over means turned over, so the transgression word is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer confesses to an old misdeed now that it is behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a noun; it is the verb to provoke. 'being over' reverses the transgression.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy or provoke them, the same as making them hostile.

clue.text: Endless petition by church about organised attendance

indicators.note: the outer pieces go about, that is around, the organised word
the petition word loses its last letter

parts.note: an appeal is a petition or plea
CE is the Church of England
to run something is to organise it, so ran means organised

explanation.surface: An unfinished church petition about the arrangements for turnout.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting in an appearance means turning up, so an appearance is an attendance at an event.

clue.text: Sailor sails sea and nautical jaunt ends

indicators.note: ends picks the final letter of each of the four words that follow sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman's outing on the water ends: sails, sea and a nautical trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt, as in 'an old salt', is informal for an experienced seaman.

clue.text: Diet's ruined with eating, eating recipe for crumble

indicators.note: the second eating means the shuffled letters close around the recipe letter
ruined says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A diet is wrecked by eating, especially eating to a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'eating' is fodder for 'ruined'; the repeated 'eating' is the container signal, wrapping the shuffled letters round the recipe abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumble is to break apart into fragments, the same as falling to pieces.

clue.text: Spun question with Arab independent republic

indicators.note: spun means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A spin doctor fields a question on Arab self-rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a republic in the Middle East.

clue.text: Screening series involving aliens, oddly

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the string word holds the other letters

parts.note: a string is a series, as in a string of wins

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of aliens

explanation.surface: A television showing of a run of episodes featuring extraterrestrials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' suggests a TV showing; here it means filtering through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Screening something through a mesh filters it, which is what passing it through a sieve does.

clue.text: Wealthy French writer mainly huge through being purchased

indicators.note: being purchased means being taken in, so the shortened writer holds the other pieces
mainly means most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Marcel Proust wrote In Search of Lost Time
OS is the abbreviation for outsize
per means through or by means of

explanation.surface: A French novelist made rich after selling hugely.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing-label size outsize; 'mainly' trims the novelist's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means flourishing financially, so a rich person is a prosperous one.

clue.text: Most prepared answer fails to oust Conservative

indicators.note: to oust means the failing word pushes out and takes the place of the Conservative letter

parts.note: to react is to answer or respond
an engine that dies fails

explanation.surface: A political reply that fails to unseat a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: DIES replaces the C in REACT.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of ready, describing whoever is most fully prepared.

clue.text: Brute's solitary end to start bird

parts.note: a pig is a coarse brute of a person

indicators.note: the last letter of the solitary word goes to its front

parts.note: one means single or solitary

explanation.surface: A brute's lonely ending brings him back to the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to start' moves the E of ONE to the front, giving EON.
explanation.definitionFit: The pigeon is a common bird, plump and grey.

clue.text: Work pressure in time leads to strike

indicators.note: the work and pressure letters go inside the time word

parts.note: a stage is a period or time, as in a stage of life
OP is short for opus, a work
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Pressure at work, given time, ends in industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work by employees, the same as industrial action.

clue.text: Fill with feed after drink

indicators.note: after says the feed word comes after the drink word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to ply someone with food is to keep feeding them

explanation.surface: Stuff oneself with food after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply a need or a post is to fill it.

clue.text: Important celebrity elevated on lot losing head

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

indicators.note: the lot word loses its first letter

parts.note: the total is the whole lot

explanation.surface: A star raised up on a film studio lot loses their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns VIP into PIV; TOTAL losing its head gives OTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Pivotal means central, the point on which everything turns, hence crucial.

clue.text: Starts to speak tentatively then finally speaks

definitions.text: Starts to speak tentatively then finally speaks

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: to utter is to speak

explanation.surface: Someone begins hesitantly and at last gets the words out.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, from the first letters of 'speak tentatively', then UTTERS; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stutters repeats opening sounds, hesitantly, before managing to say the word.

clue.text: Almost bitter split going over Kama Sutra, say

indicators.note: going over means turned over, so the pieces are read backwards
almost means the bitter word loses its last letter

parts.note: acid means sharp or bitter
tore means ripped or split

explanation.surface: A sharp quarrel splits a couple poring over an ancient sex manual.
explanation.walkthrough: ACI + TORE gives ACITORE, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is an ancient Indian text on love and sex, an example of sexual literature.

clue.text: Band going round room with cool sound

indicators.note: sound says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to freeze is to cool to ice

explanation.surface: A pop group touring a hall to a chilled-out sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians; it is a strip of decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative horizontal strip running round the walls of a room near the ceiling.

clue.text: Overhear greeting said heartlessly in study, perhaps?

indicators.note: the greeting and the outer letters of said go inside the study word
perhaps, with the question mark, admits the study word is turned round rather than given straight

parts.note: to pore over something is to study it closely
ave is the Latin greeting, hail

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle of said, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Listening in on a muttered hello in someone's private study.
explanation.walkthrough: The study word comes from the phrase 'pore over', and 'perhaps?' admits it appears turned round, split around the greeting and the ends of 'said'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to others' conversation, so it is to overhear deliberately.

clue.text: Prison objective's to change heart

indicators.note: the two middle letters of the objective word swap places

parts.note: a goal is an objective

explanation.surface: Jail's purpose is to make offenders change their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle pair of GOAL, OA, is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaol is the British spelling of jail, a prison.

clue.text: Origins of old native civilisation erased long ago

indicators.note: origins means the first letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: The roots of an ancient native culture wiped out in the distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, as in 'once upon a time'.

clue.text: Elects heads with Tory leader moving right

indicators.note: moving right means the letter shifts further along the word

parts.note: to top something is to head it

indicators.note: leader picks out the opening letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: Voters choose leaders, with the Conservative chief moving to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in TOPS shifts right, past OP.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect to do something is to choose it, so elects means chooses.

clue.text: Sailor's parrot's retired facing island before touching parting

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, so the sailor and parrot words are reversed

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
parrot's is read as parrots, and to parrot is to ape
on means touching, as in a picture on the wall

explanation.surface: A seaman's pet bird has gone into retirement on an island, a sad farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is the verb to copy; 'retired' reverses sailor and parrot together, and 'facing' and 'before' place the island and touching pieces after.
explanation.definitionFit: A parting is a separation, when people go their different ways.

clue.text: Ego of a London author

definitions.meaning: the ego is a person's sense of who they are
Will ... is a novelist and journalist from London

explanation.surface: The vanity of a writer based in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I, the person's own identity; Will Self is the London author.

clue.text: Reprobate's default overturned in time

indicators.note: the overturned word goes inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a particular time

indicators.note: overturned means read backwards

parts.note: to renege is to go back on a promise, to default

explanation.surface: A villain's broken word is reversed in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'default' is the verb to go back on a promise; 'overturned' reverses it before it goes inside the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a degenerate is a morally corrupt person, the same as a reprobate.
